description: MECHANISM: a literal `when "start"` is the ONE handler head whose body is judged statically, because the evaluator runs it synchronously at registration rather than dispatching it later (issue #1155). Measured on the evaluator: this program faults after 4 events; `repeat 2 [ when "start" [ print repcount ] ]` prints 1 then 2 and completes; and the same handler inside a procedure called from a `repeat` faults after 8 events. Meanwhile `when "stop"`, `when "START"` (event words are case-sensitive), `every`, `on_key` and `on_click` never fire in those runs, which is why their bodies stay dispatch-dependent. This fixture is the wall for a rule that treats every handler head alike — an earlier draft table-drove the four heads to close an `on_click` coverage gap and thereby asserted a uniformity it had never measured, silently losing this case. Its clean counterpart, `repeat 2 [ when "start" [ … ] ]`, is asserted in the unit suite; together they pin that the body inherits the REGISTERING context rather than being deferred.
